module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 305

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/305](https://www.erdosproblems.com/305)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [BlEr76] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., *Denominators of unit fractions*. J. Number Th. (1976),
  157-168.
- [Yo88] Yokota, H., *On a problem of Bleicher and Erdős*. J. Number Theory (1988), 198-207.
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2404.07113 (2024).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos305

/--
`D a b` is the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$.
-/
noncomputable def D (a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {B | ∃ E : Finset ℕ, 0 ∉ E ∧ (∀ n ∈ E, n ≤ B) ∧
    ∑ n ∈ E, (1 : ℚ) / n = a / b}

/-- $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. -/
noncomputable def Dmax (b : ℕ) : ℕ := (Finset.Ico 1 b).sup fun a ↦ D a b

/--
For integers $1\leq a<b$ let $D(a,b)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist
integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.$$
Estimate $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. Is it true that
$$D(b) \ll b(\log b)^{1+o(1)}?$$

Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$. If $b=p$ is a prime then
$D(p) \gg p\log p$.

This was solved by Yokota [Yo88], who proved that
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2.$$
This was improved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] to
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos305.lean#L217"]
theorem erdos_305 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto δ atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
      (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ (1 + δ b) := by
  sorry

/-- Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.bleicher_erdos : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop, (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- If $b=p$ is a prime then $D(p) \gg p\log p$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.prime_lower_bound : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → c * p * log p ≤ Dmax p := by
  sorry

/--
Yokota [Yo88] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.yokota : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
    (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * log b * log (log b) ^ 4 * log (log (log b)) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.liu_sawhney : ∃ C K : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
    (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * log b * log (log b) ^ 3 * log (log (log b)) ^ K := by
  sorry

end Erdos305

findings.description: The module docstring gives the title of reference [BlEr76] as "*Denominators of unit fractions*. J. Number Th. (1976), 157-168". The paper at J. Number Theory 8 (1976), 157–168 is actually titled "Denominators of Egyptian fractions". The file copies the wrong title word for word from erdosproblems.com's own bibliography. The mathematics is not affected. By contrast, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/321.lean cites the companion paper [BlEr76b] with the correct "Egyptian fractions" wording.
findings.source_evidence: Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar all give DOI 10.1016/0022-314X(76)90098-6 as "Denominators of Egyptian fractions", M. N. Bleicher and P. Erdős, J. Number Theory 8 (1976), 157–168. The bibliography of Liu–Sawhney (arXiv:2404.07113) reads: "[BE76] M. N. Bleicher and P. Erdős, Denominators of Egyptian fractions, J. Number Theory 8 (1976), 157–168." erdosproblems.com/latex/305 lists "[BlEr76] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _Denominators of unit fractions_. J. Number Th. (1976), 157-168.", so the slip comes from the site.
findings.suggested_fix: - [BlEr76] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., *Denominators of Egyptian fractions*. J. Number Theory 8 (1976), 157-168.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether D(b) ≪ b(log b)^{1+o(1)}. The Lean asks for δ → 0 and an explicit constant C > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large b (∀ᶠ), Dmax b ≤ C·b·(log b)^(1+δ b). So it has an extra constant and an 'eventually' quantifier.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For b large, log b > 0 and log log b > 0. Then C·(log b)^{1+δ(b)} = (log b)^{1+δ(b)+log C/log log b}, and log C/log log b → 0. So the constant can be absorbed into the o(1) exponent. Conversely, take C = 1. 'Eventually' versus 'for all b ≥ 2' makes no difference either: the finitely many small b can be absorbed by enlarging C, or by changing δ at finitely many points. I proved in Lean that the statement with C is equivalent to the statement without C, for an arbitrary f : ℕ → ℝ in place of Dmax.

reformulations.difference: The source defines D(a,b) as the least n_k over increasing sequences 1 ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k with a/b = Σ 1/n_i. The Lean takes the sInf of all caps B for which some finite set E ⊆ ℕ, with 0 ∉ E and every element ≤ B, satisfies Σ_{n∈E} 1/n = a/b in ℚ. It also has junk values: D 0 b = 0 and D a 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A Finset sorted in increasing order is exactly a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. The set of admissible caps is closed upwards, and its least element is the least possible max E. For 1 ≤ a < b the set is nonempty: every positive rational is a finite sum of distinct unit fractions (the greedy algorithm terminates). So sInf never falls back on its ∅ default. E must also be nonempty because a/b > 0. The junk inputs a = 0 and b = 0 cannot occur, because Dmax only uses 1 ≤ a < b. Sanity checks proved in Lean: `↑a / ↑b` elaborates as division in ℚ, D 1 2 = 2, and D 2 3 = 6 (so Dmax 3 = 6).

reformulations.difference: The source's (log log log b)^{O(1)} becomes ∃ K : ℝ (any sign, used as a real power), together with an extra constant C > 0 and ∀ᶠ b.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Eventually log log log b ≥ 1, so (log log log b)^{O(1)} means 'at most (log log log b)^K for some absolute constant K'. The constant C can be absorbed into K because log log log b → ∞, and allowing negative K only makes the claim stronger for that witness. So the two statements are equivalent.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization in any of the seven declarations (D, Dmax, erdos_305 and its four variants). The only finding is a cosmetic reference-title slip, which the file copied from erdosproblems.com.

**Source.** Direct curl to erdosproblems.com returned a Cloudflare JS challenge (HTTP 403) for every User-Agent I tried. I read the page and its LaTeX source (/latex/305) through the r.jina.ai reader. Every docstring in the file matches the site's LaTeX word for word.

**Statement-by-statement check against the source.**
- D and Dmax: match the site's D(a,b) and D(b) = max_{1≤a<b} D(a,b).
- erdos_305: `answer(True)` is correct, since the site says "solved in the affirmative".
- variants.bleicher_erdos: D(b) ≪ b(log b)^2. Matches the site, and Liu–Sawhney say the same.
- variants.prime_lower_bound: D(p) ≫ p log p for primes. Matches the site. I also checked it is true with an elementary argument. If N = Dmax p < p², the multiples of p up to N are p·m with m ≤ N/p < p. For a/p to be representable, some subset sum of 1/m over m ≤ N/p must be ≡ a (mod p). There are at most 2^{N/p} subset sums for p−1 values of a, so N ≥ p·log₂(p−1).
- variants.yokota: b(log b)(log log b)^4(log log log b)^2. Matches.
- variants.liu_sawhney: b(log b)(log log b)^3(log log log b)^{O(1)}. Matches Theorem thm:305 of arXiv:2404.07113.

**Lean checks.**
- `#print` shows the intended elaboration: `↑a / ↑b : ℚ`, `Real.log` everywhere, and a real-power exponent `1 + δ b`.
- Proved: `D 0 b = 0`, `Dmax 1 = 0`, `D 1 2 = 2` and `D 2 3 = 6`.
- Proved: the main statement with the constant C is equivalent to the version without it.

**Status.** Consistent everywhere. The site says PROVED and the teorth/erdosproblems database says 'proved', matching `research solved` with `answer(True)`. The `formal_proof` link (plby/lean-proofs at commit 8822f7d, line 217) proves exactly this statement, with the same definitions of D and Dmax.

**What I could not read.** The Bleicher–Erdős 1976 PDF on renyi.hu is a scanned image with no text layer, and ScienceDirect blocked automated access to Yokota's paper. The claims attributed to both are corroborated by the site and by Liu–Sawhney's LaTeX source, so this leaves no declaration unsettled.
